Why calibrated yield monitors rock as new farmer report card

Calibrating your combine’s yield monitor creates more accurate data on which to base future decisions.

Gil Gullickson,Editor,Wallaces FarmerAugust 20, 2026

schedule2 Min Read

A properly calibrated yield monitor can keep data collection humming along during harvest. Photos by Gil Gullickson

At a Glance

The accuracy of yield maps is only as good as the data that yield monitors collect. 

Multi-point calibration is superior to single-point calibration. 

It’s also crucial to keep an eye on yield monitor hardware during harvest, such as keeping sensors free of dirt and debris.

The way Luke Fuhrer sees it, a yield monitor is akin to a student report card.

“At the end of the season, you’ve made a number of different decisions — things like hybrid and varieties, herbicide programs, and fertilizer applications,” said Fuhrer, a precision agriculture engineer at Iowa State University’s Digital Ag Innovation Lab. “Of course, Mother Nature loves to throw us beautiful curveballs as well.”

The yield monitor and resulting yield maps help grade those decisions as farmers plan for subsequent growing seasons.

For that to happen, however, yield monitor calibration is key, Fuhrer said. Calibration boosts yield monitor accuracy for variable field conditions that combine operators encounter during harvest.

“It’s a little like driving when it’s sunny versus driving in storms,” Fuhrer noted. “Both are vastly different conditions, and you’ll need to drive differently between them.”

Calibration also helps improve data collection used to form field maps.

Related:Restored John Deere 730 taught farmer valuable lessons

“They are like the saying ‘garbage in, garbage out,’” Fuhrer said. “The accuracy of these field maps are only as good as the calibration.”

What to calibrate

Two key components to calibrate include:

Yield sensors. They measure the grain mass flow — yield — taken in by a combine, Fuhrer said. Calibrate for a wide moisture range, since grain moisture can alter readings. While calibrating yield sensors, adjust for machine vibration, which also can impact sensor readings.

Moisture sensors. It’s also important to calibrate moisture sensors for the large temperature swings encountered during harvest, Fuhrer said.

Calibrated yield monitors can create accurate field maps that aid in agronomic planning the following season.

Single-point vs. multi-point calibration

“Single-point calibration takes a single snapshot across a field,” Fuhrer said. “It’s a quick and easy option, and it’s better than nothing.”

Multi-point calibration is more accurate. This involves several combine passes with loads ranging from 3,000 to 6,000 pounds. Since it also involves varying speeds, it fits a wider range of simulated flow rates with the calibration curve.

Multi-point calibration also increases accuracy by creating more data points, Fuhrer said.

To ensure accurate readings, track these hardware factors during harvest, Fuhrer said:

Adjustments on a combine’s elevator chain tension. Major adjustments will require the recalibration of yield monitors.

Sensor dirt and debris accumulation. “These machines are going through very dusty and dirty conditions, so you may have to clean them throughout the season as need be,” Fuhrer said.

Feeder house lift switch obstructions. “As you drop the head down, [the switch] tells the combine, ‘We’re taking in crop, and we need to start recording data,’” Fuhrer said. “Make sure it is free of obstructions.

Related:Young farmer builds operation by upgrading old equipment

Camera lens haze and debris buildup. Clean camera lenses as needed because haze and debris affect combine automation components.

About the Author

Gil Gullickson

Editor, Wallaces Farmer

Gil Gullickson grew up on a farm that he now owns near Langford, S.D., and graduated with an agronomy degree from South Dakota State University. Earlier in his career, he spent 13 years as a Farm Progress editor, covering Minnesota and the Dakotas.

Gullickson is a widely respected and decorated ag journalist, earning the Agricultural Communicators Network writing award for Writer of the Year three times, and winning Story of the Year four times. He is a past winner of the International Federation of Agricultural Journalists’ Food and Agriculture Organization Award for Food Security. He has served as president of both ACN and the North American Agricultural Journalists.

translationZh:
在Luke Fuhrer看来，产量监测器就像学生的成绩单。

“在季节结束时，你已经做出了许多不同的决策——比如杂交品种和品种选择、除草剂方案以及施肥应用，”爱荷华州立大学数字农业创新实验室的精准农业工程师Fuhrer说道。“当然，大自然母亲也喜欢给我们抛出美丽的曲线球。”

产量监测器及由此生成的产量图有助于为这些决策评分，帮助农民规划后续种植季节。

然而，Fuhrer表示，要实现这一点，产量监测器的校准至关重要。校准能提高产量监测器在收割期间面对田间多变条件时的准确性。

“这有点像晴天驾驶与暴风雨中驾驶的区别，”Fuhrer指出。“两者是完全不同的条件，你需要以不同的方式驾驶。”

校准还有助于改进用于生成田间地图的数据收集。

“就像俗话说的‘垃圾进，垃圾出’，”Fuhrer说。“这些田间地图的准确性完全取决于校准的质量。”

**需要校准什么**

需要校准的两个关键部件包括：

产量传感器。Fuhrer说，它们测量联合收割机收获的谷物质量流量——即产量。由于谷物水分会影响读数，因此需要在较宽的水分范围内进行校准。在校准产量传感器的同时，还要调整机器振动的影响，因为振动也会影响传感器读数。

水分传感器。Fuhrer表示，针对收获期间遇到的大幅温度波动来校准水分传感器也很重要。

**单点校准与多点校准**

“单点校准是在田间取一个单一的快照，”Fuhrer说。“这是一个快速简便的选择，总比没有好。”

多点校准则更为准确。这需要联合收割机进行多次作业，每次装载量在3000到6000磅之间。由于还涉及不同的行驶速度，它能使校准曲线适应更广泛的模拟流量范围。

Fuhrer表示，多点校准还能通过创建更多数据点来提高准确性。

为了确保读数准确，Fuhrer建议在收获期间关注以下硬件因素：

联合收割机升运器链条张力的调整。重大调整将需要重新校准产量监测器。

传感器上的灰尘和碎屑积累。“这些机器在非常尘土飞扬和肮脏的条件下作业，因此你可能需要在整个季节中根据需要清洁它们，”Fuhrer说。

喂入室提升开关的阻塞。“当你放下割台时，[开关]告诉联合收割机：‘我们正在接收作物，需要开始记录数据，’”Fuhrer说。“确保它没有障碍物。”

摄像头镜头的雾化和碎屑积累。根据需要清洁摄像头镜头，因为雾化和碎屑会影响联合收割机的自动化组件。
